note: Case-law doctrine — no statutory text. Standard is entirely judge-made, grounded in interpretation of 42 U.S.C. § 1983.

primary_sources.citation: Monell v. Dept. of Social Services, 436 U.S. 658 (1978)
primary_sources.description: Foundational case establishing that municipalities are 'persons' under § 1983 and defining the policy/custom requirement for entity liability
Superseded — held municipalities were not 'persons' under § 1983; overruled by Monell
primary_sources.note: OVERRULED by Monell (1978) on the municipal liability holding

primary_sources.citation: City of Canton v. Harris, 489 U.S. 378 (1989)
primary_sources.description: Established failure-to-train as basis for municipal liability when training is so inadequate as to constitute deliberate indifference
Single decision by final policymaker can constitute official policy sufficient for Monell liability
Single incident generally insufficient to prove a custom or policy for Monell purposes

primary_sources.citation: Jett v. Dallas Independent School District, 491 U.S. 701 (1989)
primary_sources.description: Who counts as 'final policymaker' is determined by state law, not federal law
Statutory basis for Monell claims — the doctrine interprets 'person' in § 1983 to include municipalities while limiting the theory of liability
